blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Human communication involves highly coordinated multimodal signals such as speech and co-speech gestures. Existing approaches for generating both modalities commonly follow a cascaded pipeline, where speech is generated first and subsequently used to drive gesture generation; speech generation is therefore independent of gestures. We introduce Gaspard, a unified speech--gesture generation model based on continuous autoregressive generation with next-step flow-matching predictions, and trained on Seamless Interaction, a large-scale multimodal dataset. The heterogeneous temporal properties of speech and gesture motivate modality-specific prediction heads and decoupled classifier-free guidance over the two generation streams. This guidance rebalances the influence of speech and gesture at inference time, improving expressivity while mitigating dynamics collapse in continuous autoregressive gesture generation. Objective and perceptual evaluations show that Gaspard is a strong gesture generation model against unimodal baselines and that it produces highly synchronous speech and gestures compared to a matched cascaded system.
blocks.zh: 人类通信涉及高度协调的多式联运信号,如语音和同声信号。 生成这两种模式的现有办法通常采用级联式管道,首先生成语音,然后用于驱动手势生成;因此,语音生成独立于手势。 我们引入了Gaspard,一种基于连续自递式生成的统一的语音-地理生成模型,并附有下一步的流量比对预测,并接受了关于Seamless Interactive,一个大规模多式联运数据集的培训. 语音和手势的不同时间特性激发了特定模式的预测头和在两代流上解开无分类器的引导. 这种指导在推论时间重新平衡了言语和手势的影响,提高了表达性,同时在持续的自递式手势生成中缓解动态崩溃. 客观和洞察评价显示,Gaspard是对照单一模式基线的强势手势生成模式,与相应的级联系统相比,它能产生高度同步的言语和手势。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: In human communication, speech and co-speech gestures are highly coordinated signals exhibiting bidirectional dependencies: speech influences gestures and gestures influence timing [ 23 , 13 ] . For instance, gesture dynamics may be associated with changes in speech prosody, such as rhythm, pauses, pitch, or emphasis [ 14 , 40 ] . Despite such multimodal coupling, existing approaches for generating both modalities commonly rely on separate generative pipelines, where speech is first generated from text and subsequently used to condition gesture generation [ 29 ] . This design has several limitations. First, its cascaded nature requires two successive inference processes, introducing additional computational cost for real-time human-machine interactions. Second, the two modalities are modeled with a directed dependency: text drives speech, and speech drives gestures. As a consequence, gestures can adapt to speech, but cannot condition speech generation, contradicting psycholinguistic evidence of speech and gesture co-production. Unified generation therefore provides an attractive alternative, where speech and gestures are generated within the same model and can both contribute to a shared multimodal communicative state.
blocks.zh: 在人类交流中,语音和共声手势是高度协调的信号,显示双向依赖性:语音影响手势和手势影响时间[23,13]. 例如,手势动态可能与语音音速的变化有关,如节奏、暂停、投球或强调[14、40]。 尽管有这种多式联运的结合,但生成这两种模式的现有办法通常依赖单独的基因管道,其中的语音首先来自文本,然后用来作为手势生成的条件[29]。 这种设计有几个局限性. 首先,它的级联性质需要两个连续的推论过程,引入实时人机相互作用的额外计算成本. 其次,两种模式以直接依赖为模式:文本驱动语音,和语音驱动手势. 因此,手势可以适应言语,但不能对言语生成附加条件,与语言心理证据的言语和手势共同制作相矛盾. 因此,统一一代提供了一种有吸引力的替代办法,即言语和手势在同一模式内产生,既能促进共同的多式联运状态。

blocks.en: Unified speech–gesture generation, however, is not simply a matter of combining two generative processes. Speech and gestures exhibit fundamentally different temporal dynamics: speech contains rapidly varying acoustic information, whereas gestures evolve more slowly, exhibit strong temporal correlations, and often contain extended periods of limited motion. When modeled jointly, these heterogeneous dynamics can create asymmetric autoregressive dependencies, where excessive reliance on previously generated gestures progressively suppresses motion dynamics. Preserving expressive gestures while maintaining cross-modal coordination is therefore a central challenge for unified generation.
blocks.zh: 然而,统一语音-基因生成并不仅仅是两个基因过程的结合问题。 发言和手势呈现出根本不同的时间动态:发言包含迅速变化的声学信息,而手势的演化较慢,表现出强烈的时间相关性,并往往包含长时间的有限运动. 在联合建模时,这些多样的动态可以产生不对称的自递性依赖,其中过度依赖之前产生的手势逐渐抑制运动动态. 因此,在保持跨模式协调的同时保持表态姿态是统一一代人面临的一个核心挑战。

blocks.en: In this work, we introduce Gaspard (Gesture and Speech autoregressive diffusion), a continuous autoregressive model for the unified synthesis of speech and co-speech gestures from text. Gaspard performs next-step prediction in continuous speech and gesture latent spaces, with each next-step distribution modeled using flow matching.
blocks.zh: 在这部作品中,我们引入了Gaspard(Gesture and Speech autroressive spansion),这是从文本中统一合成语音和共语手势的连续自旋模型. Gaspard在连续的语音和手势潜伏空间中进行下一步的预测,每个下一步的分布模型都使用流量匹配.

blocks.en: Gaspard addresses the challenges of unified speech–gesture synthesis by jointly modeling two modalities with fundamentally different temporal dynamics. We show that these asymmetries give rise to imbalanced autoregressive feedback, leading to progressive motion collapse where gesture autoregressive history overpowers cross-modal conditioning. Inspired by compositional guidance [ 22 , 33 ] , we introduce a decoupled classifier-free guidance strategy applied to jointly generated speech and gesture streams. Unlike prior formulations that combine multiple conditioning signals for a single generated stream, our method separately regulates self-modal autoregressive feedback and cross-modal conditioning in both modalities, preserving expressive gesture dynamics while enabling tightly coordinated speech–gesture generation.
blocks.zh: Gaspard通过共同制定两种具有根本不同时间动态的模式来应对统一语音-地理综合的挑战。 我们显示,这些不对称现象导致了不平衡的自递性反馈,导致渐进运动崩溃,因为姿态自递性历史超越了跨模式条件。 在构成指导[22,33]的启发下,我们引入了适用于联合生成的语音和手势流的脱钩无分类指导策略. 与以前将多个条件信号结合用于单一生成的流的配方不同,我们的方法在两种模式中分别规范自式自递回式反馈和跨模式条件,保留了表态手势动态,同时能够进行紧密协调的语音-gesture生成.

blocks.en: Through objective and perceptual evaluations, we show that Gaspard enables controllable and expressive speech and gesture synthesis while generating both modalities in real time. We further compare Gaspard with recent unimodal gesture-generation baselines [ 28 ] and with a matched cascaded system, investigate the role of modality-specific guidance, and show that generated speech is sensitive to changes in gesture dynamics.
blocks.zh: 通过客观和洞察评估,我们显示,加斯帕德能够控制并表达言论和手势,同时实时生成两种模式。 我们进一步将Gaspard与最近的单式手势生成基准[28]和相应的级联系统进行比较,调查特定方式指导的作用,并表明生成的语音对手势动态的变化很敏感。

blocks.en: Our main contributions can be summarized as follows: • We introduce a continuous autoregressive next-step flow-matching model for joint speech–gesture generation. • We identify and characterize an autoregressive feedback imbalance in unified generation, where excessive reliance on gesture history leads to progressive motion dynamics collapse. • We adapt compositional classifier-free guidance to the autoregressive dependencies of jointly generated speech and gestures. Unlike conventional formulations that independently weight multiple conditions for a single generated stream, our decoupled CFG separately regulates self-modal and cross-modal feedback in both generation streams, mitigating gesture dynamics collapse while strengthening speech–gesture coordination.
blocks.zh: 我们的主要贡献可归纳如下: 我们为联合演讲的生成引入了连续的自递式下步流比模型。 我们确定并描述统一一代中自动反馈的不平衡,过度依赖手势历史导致渐进运动动态崩溃。 我们根据共同生成的语音和手势的自动递减依赖性,调整了无成分分类器指导. 与独立权衡单一生成的流的多种条件的常规配方不同,我们脱钩的CFG在两代流中分别调节自模式和跨模式反馈,缓解手势动态崩溃,同时加强语音-gesture协调.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Autoregressive generation of continuous data, such as speech or motion, is often performed through data discretization [ 6 , 3 , 9 , 21 , 45 ] . In this paradigm, VQ-VAEs [ 39 ] are used to quantize continuous signals into discrete codes, and the resulting code sequences are treated as tokens in an autoregressive language model. However, it also introduces an information bottleneck caused by compression and quantization, which can limit reconstruction quality [ 37 ] .
blocks.zh: 语音或运动等连续数据的自动递减生成经常通过数据磁盘化进行[6,3,9,21,45]. 在这个范式中,VQ-VAEs[39]被用来将连续的信号量化为离散代码,由此产生的代码序列在自动递归语言模型中作为符号处理. 然而,它也引入了压缩和量化导致的信息瓶颈,这可以限制重建质量[37].

blocks.en: Motivated by the success of continuous diffusion-based models, several recent works [ 20 , 37 , 38 , 34 , 32 , 43 ] have shifted toward continuous latent representations for autoregressive generation. In these approaches, autoregressive generation is typically performed through next-step diffusion over continuous codes. In particular, an autoregressive backbone predicts a conditioning representation from the preceding sequence, while a diffusion head generates the next continuous latent code.
blocks.zh: 以持续传播为基础的模型的成功为动力,最近的一些作品[20、37、38、34、32、43]已转向自动生成的持续潜在表述。 在这些方法中,自递性生成通常通过连续编码的下一步传播来实现。 特别是,一个自递性骨干会预测来自前序的调性表示,而扩散头则产生下一个连续潜在代码.

blocks.en: A common issue in autoregressive human motion synthesis is dynamics collapse, where generated motion becomes repetitive, converges toward average poses, or drifts away from the latent manifold, a phenomenon often associated with regression to the mean [ 31 ] . One approach to mitigating this issue is to reduce the model’s reliance on autoregressive motion history. During training, [ 11 ] employ high motion dropout, while [ 15 ] combine non-autoregressive pre-training with scheduled teacher forcing for co-speech gesture generation. At inference time, [ 4 ] explore reducing motion-history guidance to improve style controllability in character animation. Gaspard builds on this principle by using classifier-free guidance at inference time to balance autoregressive gesture history and speech conditioning in joint speech–gesture generation.
blocks.zh: 人类自递性运动合成中的一个常见问题是动力学崩溃,由此产生的运动变得重复,趋同为平均形式,或偏离潜在的多元形式,这种现象往往与回归到平均值[31]有关。 减轻这一问题的一个办法是减少模型对自递运动历史的依赖。 在训练期间,[11]采用高运动性退学,而[15]结合非自动前期训练与计划教师强迫进行同声手势生成. 推论时间[4]探索减少运动史指导,提高角色动画的风格可控性. Gaspard以这一原则为基础,在推论时间使用无分类器的指引,在联合语音-代词生成中平衡自递式手势历史和语音条件。

blocks.en:
A growing body of work investigates joint modeling of speech and co-speech gestures. Tacotron-ISG [ 41 ] first showed that intermediate TTS representations can effectively condition gesture generation, while Diff-TTSG [ 25 ] uses shared text representations to drive speech and gesture diffusion models. Closer coupling has also been explored by directly modeling both modalities within the same generative process. GlowTTS-ISG [ 41 ] jointly generates acoustic and motion features through a flow-based decoder, while Match-TTSG [ 24 ] adopts a single flow-matching model for speech and gesture synthesis. Recently, several works have explored full-duplex speech and gesture generation [ 26 , 42 , 27 ] . Unlike the present work, these approaches focus on modeling dyadic interactions. However, ELLSA 2 [ 42 ] also employs classifier-free guidance to enhance gesture expressivity.
Closer to our work, Gelina [ 9 ] is an autoregressive model that jointly generates discrete speech and gesture tokens through a single interleaved sequence. Its discrete gesture representation also required a flow-matching decoder to recover smooth motion, while the 75 Hz speech-token rate led to long autoregressive sequences that hindered real-time inference.
These works establish unified speech–gesture generation as a viable approach, but largely leave unexplored the cross-modal dependencies that emerge during joint generation, including how speech and gesture histories differently influence subsequent predictions.
blocks.zh:
越来越多的工作调查了联合建模的语音和共语姿态. Tacotron-ISG [41]首先显示中间TTS表示器可以有效有条件的手势生成,而Diff-TTSG [25]则使用共享文本表示器驱动语音和手势扩散模型. 还通过在同一基因过程内直接模拟两种模式,探索更紧密的结合。 GlowTTS-ISG [41]通过流体解码器联合生成声学和运动特征,而Match-TTSG [24]则采用单流匹配模型用于语音和手势合成. 最近,几部作品探索了全方位的演说和手势生成[26,42,27]. 与目前的工作不同,这些方法侧重于模拟dyadic相互作用。 然而,ELLSA 2 [42] 也采用了无分级制导,以提高手势表达性.
更接近我们的工作,Gelina[9]是一个自动递归模型,通过单个互离序列共同生成离散的语音和手势符号. 其离散的手势表示还需要一个流配调解码器来恢复平滑运动,而75赫兹的语音调速导致长时间的自旋序列阻碍实时推论.
这些作品将统一的语音代词设定为一种可行的方法,但基本上没有探讨在联合代词过程中出现的跨模式依赖性,包括语音和手势历史如何不同地影响随后的预测。

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: Gaspard generates speech and co-speech gestures from a text input, using an encoder-decoder transformer architecture. Generation can further be conditioned on an example prefix. Autoregressive prediction is performed with two separate flow-matching heads that synthesize the next-step speech and gesture embeddings. An overview of the Gaspard architecture is provided in Figure 1 .
blocks.zh: Gaspard通过文本输入生成语音和共声手势,使用编码器-解码器变压器架构. 生成还可以以示例前缀为条件. 自动递归预测用两个独立的流配头进行,将下一步的语音和手势嵌入合成. 加斯帕德建筑概况见图1。

blocks.en: Figure 1 : Gaspard generates speech and gesture continuous embeddings from text using modality-specific flow-matching heads. Speech and gesture embeddings are fused additively after modality-specific projection. At inference, a short reference prefix is provided to condition the generation, allowing both voice and gesturing style cloning.
blocks.zh: 图1 Gaspard使用特定模式的流量匹配头从文本中生成语音和手势连续嵌入. 语音和手势嵌入在模式特定投影后被添加引信。 推论中,为条件生成提供了简短的参考前缀,既允许语音,也允许调色风格克隆.

blocks.en: 3.1 Aligning speech and gesture representations
blocks.zh: 3.1 调整发言和手势说明

Specifically, we use Z-Codec [ 17 ] for speech encoding; given a speech input X s ∈ ℝ M × 1 X^{s}\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times 1} , Z-Codec encodes it into a sequence of latent embeddings denoted Z s ∈ ℝ d × N Z^{s}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times N} .
For gesture representations, we use a fully convolutional σ \sigma -VAE that takes as input a gesture sequence X g ∈ ℝ r × J × L X^{g}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times J\times L} and encodes it into a latent embedding sequence Z g ∈ ℝ d ′ × N Z^{g}\in\mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}\times N} . Both speech and gesture VAEs operate at the same latent frame rate, which simplifies downstream autoregressive modeling.

blocks.en: Speech and gesture signals, although represented in a learned latent space, exhibit different properties. Speech embeddings, for example, form a fast-varying signal, whereas gesture embeddings form a slower and more conservative signal with many repetitive patterns, for example when a limb is not used for gesturing. Figure 2 illustrates the different properties of speech and gestures.

blocks.en: The overall backbone architecture follows Gelina [ 9 ] . Text is encoded by a non-causal GLA-based encoder [ 44 ] and conditions the autoregressive decoder through cross-attention, while the causal GLA-based decoder models the fused speech-gesture history. At each autoregressive step, a binary classification head predicts whether the generation should stop.

blocks.zh: 4 实验设置

blocks.en: We trained Z-Codec’s PatchVAE, the gesture σ \sigma -VAE, and Gaspard on the Seamless Interaction dataset [ 1 ] . The public dataset contains 4,008 4,008 h of paired speech–gesture data from 4,284 4,284 participants, together with transcriptions, and is divided into naturalistic ( 2,745 2,745 h) and improvised ( 1,319 1,319 h) interactions. Speech is resampled from 48 48 to 24 24 kHz to match Z-Codec. We retain upper-body SMPL-H motion, remove leg motion and root translation, convert relative joint rotations to Rot6D [ 47 ] , and resample motion from 30 30 to 25 25 fps. Recordings are resegmented using the provided voice activity annotations, and we retain active-speaking segments only. Detailed split statistics, preprocessing parameters, and segmentation procedures are provided in Appendix 11 .

blocks.en: The backbone is a 246M-parameter encoder–decoder Transformer with gated linear attention, comprising a 6-layer text encoder, a 12-layer causal decoder, and a 1024-dimensional hidden space. Gaspard was trained for 200k steps on 2 H100 GPUs using bf16 mixed-precision, corresponding to approximately 40 h of training. The pretrained speech and gesture autoencoders are kept frozen during this training stage. At inference time, we use 15 15 flow-matching sampling steps for both the speech and gesture heads. Full architecture and optimizer configurations are provided in Appendix 12 .

We conduct our evaluation on two evaluation subsets of the test split of the Seamless Interaction dataset. The comparison against gesture-generation baselines is performed on a manually curated subset used in the Genea Challenge [ 28 ] , referred to as Genea-95 (95 segments). We also include an automatically curated subset, Seamless-416 , containing 416 416 segments from 93 93 speakers, for a total duration of approximately 2 2 h 35 35 min. Evaluation recordings range from 15 15 to 35 35 s. For each speaker, a unique separate segment of at most 10 10 s is selected as a speech and gesture prefix for generation.
We provide additional details regarding segment selection, curation, and other processing steps in Appendix 14.1 .

blocks.en:
At the time of the research and to the best of our knowledge, there exist no open-source unified speech and gesture generation models trained on the Seamless Interaction dataset. Because of differing pose representations (rotations/positions, considered limbs, etc.), adapting existing models to the dataset would require substantial engineering efforts. We therefore compare Gaspard against recent unimodal speech-driven gesture generation models: UNICAMP [ 36 ] , GestFlow [ 10 ] , DyaSync-Sem [ 8 ] , and UM-FERI [ 7 ] , trained on Seamless Interaction and evaluated in the Genea Challenge 2026 [ 28 ] . These baselines use ground-truth speech originating from the dataset, whereas Gaspard generates both the speech and the gestures from text. We additionally compare Gaspard against the teacher-version of PocketTTS [ 34 ] , a 350M-parameter continuous autoregressive TTS model, which we trained on the Seamless Interaction dataset. We finally construct a Cascaded baseline combining a unimodal text-to-speech model with a speech-driven gesture generation model, which follows the same training recipe as Gaspard. Its TTS component corresponds exactly to Gaspard, without gesture embedding inputs and gesture flow-matching head. The speech-driven gesture generation component follows the Gaspard architecture, except that the speech objective weight, λ s \lambda_{\mathrm{s}} in Equation 4 , is set to 0.0001 0.0001 and kept only for regularization purposes. All remaining architectural components and training settings are kept unchanged.
We provide additional details about the baseline models in Appendix 12.4 .

在研究时,据我们所知,在无缝互动数据集方面没有受过培训的开源统一语音和手势生成模型。 由于姿势不同(旋转/姿势、被视为四肢等),对现有模型进行调整以适应数据集需要大量工程工作。 因此,我们比较了Gaspard与最近的单式语音驱动手势生成模型:UNICAMP[36]、GestFlow[10]、DyaSync-Sem[8]和UM-FERI[7],这些模型接受了无缝互动培训,并在Genea挑战2026[28]中得到了评价。 这些基线使用源于数据集的地面真言,而Gaspard则同时生成来自文本的语音和手势. 我们还将Gaspard与PocketTTS[34]的教师版本进行比较,PocketTTS是一个350M参数的连续自转TTS模型,我们在无缝相互作用数据集上进行了训练. 我们最终构建了一个Cascad的基线,将单模式文本对语音模式与语音驱动的手势生成模式结合起来,后者遵循了与Gaspard相同的训练方法。 它的TTS组件与Gaspard完全对应,没有手势嵌入输入和手势流量匹配头. 语音驱动的手势生成组件遵循Gaspard架构,只不过在方程式4中,语音的客观权重Qλ s\lambda_{\ mathrm{s}},设定为0.0001 0.0001,仅用于规范化目的. 所有剩余的建筑构件和培训环境保持不变。

blocks.en:
We evaluate speech and gesture synthesis separately. Gesture metrics include Fréchet Gesture Distance (FGD) [ 46 ] , Beat Consistency (BC) [ 19 ] , and ℓ 1 \ell_{1} -Diversity [ 21 ] . To complement FGD and inspired by [ 30 ] , we introduce kinetic Fréchet Gesture Distance, denoted by FGD k \mathrm{FGD}_{k} . Rather than comparing latent features directly, FGD k \mathrm{FGD}_{k} compares distributions of first-order temporal variations in the latent space. Appendix 13 describes and validates the metric.
FGD measures pose-distribution similarity, whereas FGD k \mathrm{FGD}_{k} aims to capture motion dynamics similarities. BC measures speech–gesture synchrony, and diversity measures motion variability. For speech, we report Word Error Rate (WER), UTMOS [ 35 ] , and Speaker Similarity (SS) computed with WavLM [ 5 ] . We also report real-time factor (RTF).

blocks.en: We conducted two perceptual studies, one for comparison against gesture generation baselines and one for our ablation study. For both studies, all stimuli were rendered in Blender using the 3D scene and avatar representations used in the Genea Leaderboard [ 16 ] . The average duration of the stimuli is 20 s. Participants recruited through Prolific evaluated 30 30 randomly sampled stimuli on a 1 1 – 5 5 Likert scale and completed two attention checks. Human-likeness of gestures was evaluated from muted videos; speech–gesture synchronization was evaluated from audiovisual stimuli. The ablation study additionally evaluated voice human-likeness from audio alone. The evaluation subsets and participant groups differed between studies, as specified below and further detailed in Appendix 14.1 . For both studies, participant-level MOS were analyzed with repeated-measures ANOVA and Holm-corrected pairwise tests.

blocks.en: 6 Discussion
blocks.zh: 讨论

blocks.en:
The results show that the proposed method is a strong approach for expressive behavior synthesis. Gaspard outperforms unimodal gesture-generation baselines in objective and perceptual evaluations while generating both speech and gestures. Although Gaspard generates intelligible speech, it underperforms against PocketTTS. We hypothesize that the larger number of parameters for PocketTTS (350M) compared to Gaspard (246M), and the use of Mimi, a strong audio codec, can explain these differences. Since Gaspard generates slightly lower quality speech than its cascaded counterpart, it is also possible that generating gestures jointly with speech may deteriorate speech quality. In contrast, unified generation produces highly synchronous and human-like speech and gesture behaviors, as demonstrated by the perceptual results.
Objective and perceptive results also indicate that decoupled CFG rebalances the impact of each modality during next-step prediction. Reducing γ g G \gamma_{g}^{G} weakens the contribution of gesture history, mitigating dynamics collapse, while increasing γ s G \gamma_{s}^{G} strengthens speech conditioning.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion and Limitations
blocks.zh: 7. 结论和限制

blocks.en:
We presented Gaspard, a speech and gesture generation model, and we a introduced modality-decoupled CFG strategy that separately controls speech and gesture conditioning. We show that unified generation achieves leading perceptual performance, and decoupled guidance makes continuous autoregressive gesture generation expressive and mitigates dynamics collapse while improving speech-driven gesture dynamics. Compared with its cascaded counterpart, Gaspard achieves stronger gesture dynamics, perceptual gesture quality, synchronization, and lower inference time, while the cascaded system retains advantages on several unimodal objective metrics.
Limitations include the computational cost of multiple guidance passes, and evaluations of long-term generation and out-of-domain generalization remain important future work.

blocks.en: Generative AI tools were used to assist with coding, language polishing, and the summarization of research notes. blocks.en: This work primarily involved computational experiments and anonymous, non-invasive perceptual studies with consenting adult participants, for which formal ethical approval was not required under the applicable institutional guidelines. User studies were performed on the Prolific platform. Participants were all older than 18 y.o and fairly compensated. All datasets were used in accordance with their respective licenses, and the user studies were conducted with informed consent and fair participant compensation. Cloning experiments were restricted to speakers who had provided consent, and public demonstrations include safeguards intended to mitigate potential misuse.

blocks.en: The models together with their trained parameters will be made publicly available. While this facilitates reproducibility and enables further research, it also makes these models accessible for unintended or potentially harmful applications. In particular, because the proposed models aim to synthesize realistic human speech and behavior, they could be misused to generate convincing deepfakes, impersonate individuals, or create synthetic content without the consent of the people being represented.

blocks.en: 11.1 Dataset composition
blocks.zh: 11.1 数据集组成

blocks.en: Seamless Interaction contains 4,065 4,065 h of paired speech–gesture data from 4,284 4,284 participants, with associated transcriptions. Participants are recorded during dyadic interactions. The dataset is divided into two main parts: naturalistic ( 2,745 2,745 h) and improvised ( 1,319 1,319 h). In the naturalistic part, one participant is given a script to anchor the topic of the discussion, while the other is asked to behave naturally. This split contains spontaneous interactions but also many low-dynamics segments. In the improvised part, each participant is given a role-play prompt, leading to more expressive interactions, although less natural. The naturalistic and improvised subsets exhibit different levels of expressive motion.
blocks.zh: 无缝互动包含来自4,284,4284名参与者的4,065,4,065 h配对语音-地理学数据,并附有相关的抄录. 参与者在对话互动中记录。 数据集主要分为两个部分:自然论(2,745,2,745 h)和即兴论(1,319,319 h). 在自然主义部分,一位参与者得到一个脚本来固定讨论的主题,而另一位参与者则被要求自然行事. 这种分裂包含自发的相互作用,但也包含许多低动力片段. 在即兴部分中,给每个参与者一个角色扮演的迅速性,导致更多的表现性互动,尽管不那么自然. 自然主义和简易子集表现出不同程度的表达运动.

blocks.en: 11.2 Speech, gesture, and text preprocessing
blocks.zh: 11.2 发言、手势和文字预处理

blocks.en: Speech is provided as a waveform at 48 48 kHz. We resample it to 24 24 kHz for data compression and to match the sample rate required by Z-Codec. Gestures are represented as full-body SMPL-H pose sequences at 30 30 fps. Motion in Seamless Interaction is obtained through pseudo-mocap estimation from three simultaneous cameras. As a result, some sequences contain pose-estimation artifacts caused by occlusions, limb contacts, or interactions with surrounding objects. These artifacts can create unrealistic dynamics and discontinuities. Because all interactions were recorded in the same setting, with participants standing on a recording pod, we remove leg motion and root translation and model upper-body gestures only. Motion sequences are then resampled to 25 25 fps to match the input rate of the gesture encoder.
blocks.zh: 发言以波形形式提供,时间48千赫。 我们把它重新做成24 24kHz的数据压缩,并匹配Z-Codec所需的样本速率. 手势作为全身SMPL-H姿势序列在30英尺高度时被代表. 在无缝相互作用中的运动是通过三个同时相机的伪摩卡普估计得到的. 因此,一些序列中包含由吞噬,肢体接触,或与周围物体的相互作用导致的姿势估计文物. 这些文物可以产生不切实际的动态和不连续性. 因为所有的相互作用都是在同一场合记录的,参与者站在一个录音舱上,所以我们只去掉了腿运动和根部翻译以及模型上体手势. 运动序列随后被重印到25个25英尺的高度,以配合手势编码器的输入速率.

blocks.en: The SMPL-H body model represents body poses as a skeleton of relative joint rotations. We convert these rotations to Rot6D [ 47 ] , a representation known to be better suited to learning-based modeling. Gesture segments are therefore represented as sequences G ∈ ℝ J × 6 × N G\in\mathbb{R}^{J\times 6\times N} , where J = 43 J=43 is the number of body joints considered and N N is the sequence length. Following [ 1 ] , we apply a Savitzky–Golay filter using a 9 9 -frame window and a polynomial order of 3 3 . This filtering reduces motion jerk without over-smoothing rapid gestures. For text, we use the provided transcriptions, obtained with WhisperX [ 2 ] , together with the voice activity annotations. We do not apply the filter to evaluation segments.
blocks.zh: SMPL-H体型代表身体作为相对联轴旋转的骨架. 我们把这些旋转转换成Rot6D[47],这个代表已知更适合以学习为基础的模型. 因此,手腕部分作为序列G ∈ R J × 6×N G\in\mathb{R\J\times 6\times N},其中J=43J=43是考虑的体关节数,NN为序列长度. 在[1]之后,我们采用Savitzky-Golay滤波器,使用一个9 9 帧窗口和3 3 的多名顺序。 这种过滤会减少运动混蛋,而不会产生过度的快速姿态. 对于文字,我们使用所提供的抄本,用WhisperX[2]获得,连同语音活动说明. 我们不对评价部分使用过滤器。

blocks.en: 11.3 Dataset segmentation
blocks.zh: 11.3 数据集分割

blocks.en: Segments in Seamless Interaction have variable durations, typically ranging from 2 2 to 10 10 min. These durations are substantially longer than the segments typically used to train TTS models, which are usually around 30 30 to 60 60 s. To stabilize training and improve efficiency, in particular by reducing padding and enabling length-bucketed data loading, we resegment each speech–gesture recording using the voice activity detection annotations.
blocks.zh: 无缝相互作用中的片段有可变持续时间,一般从2,2到10,10分钟不等. 这些持续时间大大长于通常用于训练TTS型号的区段,通常在30至60秒左右. 为了稳定培训和提高效率,特别是通过减少粘贴和允许长插数据加载,我们利用语音活动检测说明重新对每个语音-gesture记录进行分类。

blocks.en: Each original recording corresponds to a full dyadic interaction, so a given participant can alternate between speaking and listening. While recent work [ 26 ] shows that a model can explicitly represent this interactive state, we focus on active-speaking segments only.
blocks.zh: 每个原声录音都对应一个完整的dyadic交互,因此给定的参与者可以在演讲和聆听之间交替. 虽然最近的工作[26]表明一个模型可以明确代表这种互动状态,但我们只关注活跃语段.

blocks.en: The variance structure of the latent space is critical for autoregressive next-step diffusion, since sampling uncertainty accumulates over generation steps [ 37 ] . However, standard VAEs are prone to variance collapse, an optimization phenomenon where the predicted variance of some channels collapses to 0, making the VAE practically deterministic in some dimensions. blocks.en: 13.2 FGD feature extractor
blocks.zh: 13.2 FGD 特性提取器

blocks.en: Unlike BEAT2, Seamless Interaction does not provide a pretrained feature extractor suitable for computing FGD. We therefore train a non-causal VAE. The feature extractor encodes gesture sequences sampled at 30 30 fps into continuous latent embeddings at 7.5 7.5 Hz, with a latent dimensionality of 40 40 . The architecture is not primarily designed to maximize frame-level reconstruction accuracy. Instead, its temporal compression and relatively compact latent space encourage the aggregation of motion information into semantically meaningful representations, which is more appropriate for distribution-level evaluation with FGD. The feature extractor is trained on the improvised training split, and the evaluated segments are not seen during training.
blocks.zh: 与BEAT2不同的是,无缝相互作用不提供适合计算FGD的前置特性提取器. 因此,我们训练一个非原因的VAE。 特性提取器将30英尺30英尺的手势序列编码成7.5赫兹的连续潜嵌,潜在维度为4040。 建筑设计主要不是为了最大限度地实现帧级重建的准确性. 相反,其时间压缩和相对紧凑的潜在空间鼓励将运动信息集成成具有实质意义的表述,这更适合与FGD进行分布级评价. 特征提取器接受简易培训分期培训,培训期间没有看到经过评估的部分。

blocks.en: Conventional FGD compares the distribution of extracted latent features but does not explicitly characterize how these features evolve over time. Two sets of sequences may therefore exhibit similar feature distributions while differing substantially in motion amplitude, smoothness, or temporal variability. This limitation is particularly relevant for autoregressive models, which may produce realistic individual poses while suffering from over-smoothed, static, or locally unstable motion dynamics.
blocks.zh: 常规FGD比较了提取的潜在特征的分布情况,但没有明确描述这些特征如何随时间演变。 因此,两组序列可能呈现类似的特征分布,但在运动振幅、光滑度或时间变异方面则大不相同。 这种限制与自递性模型特别相关,因为自递性模型可能会产生现实的个人姿势,而同时又会受到过度散乱、静态或局部不稳定的运动动态的影响。

blocks.en: 13.3 Validation of kinetic FGD
blocks.zh: 13.3 动力学FGD的验证

blocks.en: To validate the sensitivity of FGD k \mathrm{FGD}_{k} to the motion dynamics, we computed FGD and FGD k \mathrm{FGD}_{k} on the clean test set after applying controlled perturbations to the original gesture sequences: • We modified the velocity of gesture sequences through temporal interpolation or downsampling. • We smoothed the original gesture sequences using a Savitzky-Golay filter, and varied the filter window size to progressively increase the smoothness. • We altered the original gesture sequences by adding a jerk component, defined as the difference between the original and smoothed motion and scaled by a factor controlling the perturbation magnitude.

blocks.zh: 我们通过时间插图或下采样修改了手势序列的速度。

blocks.en: We smoothed the original gesture sequences using a Savitzky-Golay filter, and varied the filter window size to progressively increase the smoothness.
blocks.zh: 我们用萨维茨基-戈莱过滤器平滑了原始的手势序列,并修改了过滤窗口大小,以逐渐提高光滑度.

blocks.en: We altered the original gesture sequences by adding a jerk component, defined as the difference between the original and smoothed motion and scaled by a factor controlling the perturbation magnitude.
blocks.zh: 我们修改了原来的手势序列,增加了一个混蛋组件,定义是原运动和平滑运动的区别,并用一个控制扰动量的因素来缩放.

blocks.en: As shown in Figure 11 , changes in gesture speed, smoothness and jerk have little effect on FGD, whereas FGD k {\mathrm{FGD}_{k}} is much more sensitive to these temporal variations. Notably, FGD remains very low despite modified gesture velocity.

blocks.en: Figure 11 : We validate the FGD k \mathrm{FGD}_{k} metric by varying gesturing velocity ( Top ), smoothness ( Middle ) and jerk ( Bottom ). We also include the BC score corresponding to all three perturbations. FGD shows little sensitivity to the perturbations, whereas FGD k \mathrm{FGD}_{k} captures velocity, smoothness and jerk variations.

blocks.en: 13.4 Beat Consistency calibration
blocks.zh: 13.4 国家 击败一致性校准

blocks.en: Because the motion dynamics and pose distributions of Seamless Interaction differ substantially from those of BEAT2, the hyperparameters of the Beat Consistency metric require dataset-specific calibration. We adjust the velocity–acceleration threshold used for gesture-stroke detection and the parameter σ \sigma , which controls the temporal tolerance of the alignment function. These parameters are empirically set to 0.25 0.25 and 0.3 0.3 , respectively. We select this configuration by maximizing the difference in BC score between correctly aligned speech–gesture pairs and artificially misaligned pairs, thereby ensuring that the metric discriminates between synchronized and unsynchronized sequences on Seamless Interaction.
blocks.zh: 由于无缝相互作用的运动动力学和姿势分布与BEAT2大相径庭,Beat一致性度量衡的超参数需要数据集特定的校准. 我们调整用于手势-中程检测的速度-加速阈值, 以及控制对齐函数时间耐力的参数\\sigma 。 这些参数按经验分别设定为0.250.25和0.30.3。 我们选择这种配置的方式是,将BC 的分数差异最大化,在对齐的语音 - gesture 配对和人为的错配配对之间,从而确保在无缝相互作用上,量子区分同步序列和非同步序列。

blocks.en: A limitation of BC is that temporally unstable or jerky motion may also produce a high score, as rapid motion variations increase the number of detected gesture beats and therefore the likelihood of alignment with speech beats. BC should consequently not be interpreted independently, but jointly with FGD and FGD k \mathrm{FGD}_{k} , which respectively evaluate the realism of the gesture representations and their latent dynamics. We illustrate this effect in Figure 11 .
blocks.zh: BC的一个局限性是,时间不稳定或干燥的运动也可能产生很高的分数,因为快速的运动变化会增加检测到的手势节拍的次数,从而增加与语音节拍一致的可能性. 因此,巴塞尔公约不应单独解释,而应与FGD和FGD k\mathrm{FGD}_{k}联合解释,后者分别评估手势表现的现实性及其潜在的动态。 我们在图11中说明了这一效果。

blocks.en: 13.5 WER

For WER computation, we used WhisperX [ 2 ] to obtain speech transcriptions and applied peak normalization to the input audio. Both the ground-truth recordings and the generated samples were transcribed using this ASR. Since the speech segments from the Seamless Interaction dataset originate from spontaneous dyadic interactions, it is important to note that the reference transcriptions may contain inconsistencies. In particular, some ground-truth recordings contain speech leakage (i.e. the interlocutor’s speech) or background noise from the interlocutor, which may also be transcribed by the ASR system. This difference from the clean, studio-recorded data commonly used for TTS evaluation partly explains why the reported WER scores remain relatively high compared with state-of-the-art TTS systems.
blocks.zh: 对于WER计算,我们使用WhisperX[2]来获取语音转录,并对输入音频进行峰值正常化. 地面真实录音和生成的样品都使用这一ASR进行转录。 由于来自无缝相互作用数据集的语音部分源于自发的dyadic相互作用,因此必须指出,参考资料抄录可能包含不一致之处。 特别是,一些地面真实录音含有语音泄漏(即对话者的发言)或对话者的背景噪音,这些声音也可能由ASR系统转录。 与TTS评价常用的清洁、录音室记录数据不同,部分地解释了为什么所报告的WER分数与最先进的TTS系统相比仍然较高。

blocks.en: 14 Evaluation protocol details
blocks.zh: 14 评价协议细节

blocks.en: 14.1 Construction of the Seamless-416 evaluation subset
blocks.zh: 14.1 无缝416评价子集的构建

blocks.en:
Since the original Seamless Interaction test split is relatively large (approximately 60 60 h), we construct a smaller subset for evaluation. The candidate subset contains recordings ranging from 15 15 to 35 35 s and initially covers 103 103 speakers from the raw test set of Seamless Interaction. For each speaker, we additionally select a random shorter segment with a maximum duration of 10 10 s, which is used as a speech and gesture prefix for Gaspard generation. These prefixes do not overlap with the evaluated segments.
A substantial number of candidate segments present limited motion or insufficient speech quality. To ensure a fair and meaningful evaluation, we initially sample 487 487 segments from the test split, corresponding to approximately four to six segments per speaker. We then exclude unsuitable segments and prefixes according to the following criteria: • We retain only segments with a static gesture ratio below 50 % 50\% , ensuring that evaluated sequences are non-static and contain meaningful gestures. • We discard segments containing unintelligible speech caused by recording issues. • We discard segments for which the provided transcription does not match the recorded speech.
blocks.zh:
由于最初的无缝相互作用试验分裂相对较大(约60 h),我们构建了一个较小的子集来进行评估. 候选子集收录的录音从15个15个到35个35个s不等,最初覆盖了来自原始测试集"无缝相互作用"的103个103个发言者. 对于每个发言者,我们额外选择一个最短的随机段,最长长度为10 10 s,用作Gaspard一代的演讲和手势前缀. 这些前缀不与被评价的片段重叠.
大量候选人部分动议有限或发言质量不足。 为了确保公平和有意义的评价,我们最初抽取了487 487段的试题,相当于每个发言者大约4至6段。 然后,我们根据以下标准排除不适当的部分和前缀: 我们只保留静态手势比低于50%的区段,确保评估的序列是非静态的,并包含有意义的手势。 · 我们放弃录制问题导致的含不通晓的言论的片段。 我们丢弃那些与录音发言不符的片段。

blocks.en: We retain only segments with a static gesture ratio below 50 % 50\% , ensuring that evaluated sequences are non-static and contain meaningful gestures.
blocks.zh: 我们只保留静态手势比低于50%的区段,确保评估的序列是非静态的,并包含有意义的手势。

blocks.en: We discard segments containing unintelligible speech caused by recording issues.
blocks.zh: 我们丢弃那些由录音问题引起的 无法理解的演讲部分。

blocks.en: This screening is performed exclusively on ground-truth human recordings and is not based on the performance of the evaluated models. The resulting clean test subset contains 416 416 segments from 93 93 speakers, corresponding to a total duration of approximately 2 2 h 35 35 min. The complete list of selected files and their corresponding timestamps will be made publicly available to support reproducibility.

blocks.en: 14.2 Seamless-416 user study
blocks.zh: 14.2 无缝416用户研究

blocks.en: We constructed the user study evaluation set by randomly sampling 13 13 speakers from the Seamless-416 subset. For each of the speakers, we selected up to four segments of 15 15 – 35 35 seconds, discarding segments containing pose glitches or unintelligible speech; this screening is performed solely based on the recordings from the dataset. The resulting evaluation set consists of 24 24 segments from 11 11 speakers, including 4 4 males and 7 7 females.
blocks.zh: 我们通过随机抽样从无缝416子集中抽取13个发言者,构建了用户研究评价。 我们为每位发言者选择了最多4个15至35秒的片段,丢弃含有姿势缺陷或无法理解的演讲的片段;这种放映完全根据数据集的录音进行。 评估由11名发言者的24个24个部分组成,其中包括4名男性和7名女性。

blocks.en: All evaluated systems used their generated speech and gestures. Differences in perceived synchrony may therefore originate from variations in speech and variations in gestures. Isolating either, by fixing one modality input, is possible but out of the scope of the present research and is left for future investigations.
blocks.zh: 所有被评价的系统都使用了其生成的语音和手势. 因此,感觉同步性的差异可能源于语音和手势的差异。 通过确定一种模式输入,将两者隔离是可能的,但不属于目前研究的范围,留待将来调查。

blocks.en: 14.3 Genea-95 evaluation subset
blocks.zh: 14.3 Genea-95评价子集

blocks.en:
The Genea Challenge 2026 performed a benchmark evaluation on a manually curated subset of the test set of Seamless Interaction. The evaluation set provided by the organizers contains 95 95 segments in the public subset and 83 83 in the private subset.
Because the human recordings are not available for the private subset, we only consider the public one.
For each speaker, we manually selected a short segment with a maximum duration of 10 10 s from the test set of the Seamless Interaction dataset. We discarded prefixes containing glitches or unintelligible speech. The prefixes do not overlap with the evaluated segments.
There is no overlap between the Genea-95 and the Seamless-416 evaluation sets.
blocks.zh:
Genea Challenge 2026对测试集"无缝互动"中手工整理的子集进行了基准评价. 组织者提供的一套评价包含95个公共子集和83个私人子集。
因为人类的录音不能提供给私人片段 我们只考虑公开片段

blocks.en: Because Gaspard is conditioned by a short speech-gesture prefix, the synthesis may contain more speaker-specific information than the baselines. We do acknowledge that it might affect the fairness of the evaluation. Though, this conditioning can be seen as a sort of speaker-embedding, a common strategy in gesture generation systems. blocks.en: 15.1 Inference efficiency

blocks.en: We investigate Gaspard’s inference efficiency by varying the number of flow-matching sampling steps. Figure 12 shows that increasing the number of sampling steps generally improves both speech and gesture generation quality, at the cost of increased inference time. Increasing the number of steps from 10 10 to 30 30 raises the RTF from 0.63 0.63 to 1.33 1.33 . In all experiments, we therefore use 15 15 sampling steps as a compromise between generation quality and real-time efficiency, corresponding to an RTF of 0.84 0.84 .

blocks.en: 15.3 Speech adaptation to gesture
blocks.zh: 15.3 言论适应姿态

blocks.en: One key motivation for generating speech and gesture jointly is to allow the generation of each modality to be conditioned on the other. To analyze the influence of gestures on speech generation, we conducted controlled experiments in which a ground-truth gesture sequence was imposed on the gesture stream while the model generated the corresponding speech. We then modified the kinematic properties of this conditioning gesture input, in particular its speed, while keeping the input text unchanged. This setting allows us to examine how changes in gesture kinematics influence the generated speech. We did not constrain the duration of the generated speech. For each condition, generation ends once the complete input text has been synthesized. If the input gesture sequence ends before speech generation is complete, the model resumes joint autoregressive generation of both speech and gesture until the full input text is generated.
blocks.zh: 共同产生言论和手势的一个关键动机是使每种方式的产生受到另一种条件的限制。 为了分析手势对语音生成的影响,我们进行了有控制的实验,在模型产生相应语音的同时,手势流上也施加了地面真实手势序列. 然后我们修改了这种调制手势输入的动能特性,特别是其速度,同时保持输入文本不变. 这个设定让我们可以检查手势动能的变化如何影响生成的语音. 我们没有限制演讲的时间。 对于每个条件,一旦完整输入文本被合成,生成就结束. 如果输入手势序列在语音生成完成前结束,该模型恢复语音和手势的联合自动生成,直到生成完整的输入文本.

blocks.en: For this experiment, we selected 31 31 samples from the test set, covering 8 8 different speaker identities. For each sample, we generated two speech sequences using two different random seeds and the same input text. Speech generation was conditioned on temporally scaled versions of the corresponding gesture sequence, using speed multipliers in [ 0.8 , 0.9 , 1 , 1.1 , 1.2 ] [0.8,0.9,1,1.1,1.2] . As a result, each speed multiplier corresponds to 62 62 generated speech sequences, obtained from 31 31 distinct gesture–text pairs.
blocks.zh: 为了这个实验,我们从测试集中挑选了31个样本,涵盖了8个不同的扬声器身份. 对于每个样本,我们利用两个不同的随机种子和相同的输入文本生成两个语音序列. 语音生成以相应手势序列的时间缩放版本为条件,使用速度乘数在[0.8,0.9,1,1.1,1.2] [0.8,0.9,1,1.1,1.2]. 因此,每个速度乘数对应62个生成的语音序列,从31个不同的手势-文本对获得.

blocks.en: We report the evolution of the average speech rate and inter-pausal unit (IPU) number, together with their corresponding median Spearman correlation coefficient, in Figure 13 . Speech rate is computed as the number of syllables per second. An IPU corresponds to a stretch of speech boudned by pauses. An IPU is detected when a speaker remains silent for at least 0.2 0.2 s. Progressively increasing gesturing speed increases the average speech rate from 3.27 3.27 syllables/s to 4.03 4.03 syllables/s while decreasing the average number of IPUs from around 10 10 to below 8 8 . Both the variations in speech rate and IPU number exhibit a fairly strong correlation as indicated by a median Spearman correlation coefficient of ρ = 0.7 \rho=0.7 and ρ = − 0.6 \rho=-0.6 respectively.
